classification.difficultyReason: Distinguishes absolute values applied to outputs and inputs, combines both operations, and recognises when positivity leaves an exponential unchanged.

content.prompt: Sketch, on separate axes, the graphs of:

answer.short: Minimum $(1,0)$; passes through $(\tfrac12,1)$, $(2,1)$ and $(4,2)$. Vertical asymptote $x=0$. Domain $(0,\infty)$; range $[0,\infty)$.
answer.worked:
Retain the part of $y=\log_2x$ above the $x$-axis and reflect its negative part in the $x$-axis.

$$y=\begin{cases}-\log_2x,&0<x<1,\\\log_2x,&x\ge1.\end{cases}$$

The branches meet at $(1,0)$. Both $y\to\infty$ as $x\to0^+$ and $y\to\infty$ as $x\to\infty$.

spec.description: Equation-driven sketch of the absolute value of the base-two logarithm, with key-value guides.
spec.mathematics: y=abs(log(x)/log(2)), x>0; minimum (1,0); vertical asymptote x=0.

answer.short: $y=2^x$: increasing through $(-1,\tfrac12)$, $(0,1)$, $(1,2)$ and $(2,4)$, with horizontal asymptote $y=0$. Domain $\mathbb R$; range $(0,\infty)$.
answer.worked: Since $2^x>0$ for every real $x$, $|2^x|=2^x$. Sketch the usual increasing exponential through $(-1,\tfrac12)$, $(0,1)$, $(1,2)$ and $(2,4)$. The curve approaches the $x$-axis as $x\to-\infty$.

spec.description: Unchanged positive exponential with guides to the source answer's key values.

answer.short: Two branches symmetric about the $y$-axis, through $(\pm1,0)$, $(\pm2,1)$ and $(\pm\tfrac12,-1)$. Vertical asymptote $x=0$. Domain $\mathbb R\setminus\{0\}$; range $\mathbb R$.
answer.worked:
Retain $y=\log_2x$ for $x>0$ and reflect this branch in the $y$-axis to obtain the branch for $x<0$.

$$y=\begin{cases}\log_2(-x),&x<0,\\\log_2x,&x>0.\end{cases}$$

Both branches approach $-\infty$ as $x\to0$, and rise without bound as $|x|\to\infty$.

spec.description: Two logarithmic branches symmetric about the vertical axis.
spec.mathematics: y=log_2(abs(x)); zeros at plus and minus 1; asymptote x=0.

answer.short: Symmetric about the $y$-axis, with minimum $(0,1)$, through $(\pm1,2)$ and $(\pm2,4)$. Domain $\mathbb R$; range $[1,\infty)$.
answer.worked:
Retain the right-hand half of $y=2^x$ and reflect it in the $y$-axis.

$$y=\begin{cases}2^{-x},&x<0,\\2^x,&x\ge0.\end{cases}$$

The branches meet at $(0,1)$, pass through $(\pm1,2)$ and $(\pm2,4)$, and rise without bound in both directions. There is no asymptote.

spec.description: Reflected positive-input exponential branches meeting at a sharp minimum.

answer.short: Symmetric about the $y$-axis, with minima $(\pm1,0)$, through $(\pm\tfrac12,1)$ and $(\pm2,1)$. Vertical asymptote $x=0$. Domain $\mathbb R\setminus\{0\}$; range $[0,\infty)$.
answer.worked:
First sketch $y=\log_2|x|$ by reflecting the positive-input logarithmic branch in the $y$-axis. Then reflect every part below the $x$-axis upwards.

$$y=\begin{cases}-\log_2|x|,&0<|x|<1,\\\log_2|x|,&|x|\ge1.\end{cases}$$

The two minima are $(\pm1,0)$. The curve rises without bound as $x\to0^\pm$ and as $|x|\to\infty$.

spec.description: Four equation-driven pieces forming two minima and an upward vertical asymptote.

answer.short: $y=2^{|x|}$, the same graph as part d: minimum $(0,1)$, symmetry about the $y$-axis and points $(\pm1,2)$, $(\pm2,4)$. Domain $\mathbb R$; range $[1,\infty)$.
answer.worked: Since $2^{|x|}>0$, the outer absolute value changes nothing. Retain the right-hand half of $y=2^x$ and reflect it in the $y$-axis. Draw both branches meeting at $(0,1)$, passing through $(\pm1,2)$ and $(\pm2,4)$ and rising without bound. There is no asymptote.
